source_review.notes: Checked the primary DRF, Jain fairness-index, Mesos, and Borg publications plus current Apache Hadoop, Spark, Mesos, and Kubernetes documentation. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Formal fairness properties are scoped to their models; product behavior and configuration are explicitly attributed.

evidence: Reviewed resource dimensions D, totals R, subject demand a, allocation x, weight w, entitlement g, maximum M, dominant share s, normalized service z, Jain index J, and temporal resource-service X.
Checked CPU, GiB, percentages, resource fractions, resource-time, weights, demands, and allocations retain consistent scopes and units.
Checked fair share, guarantee, maximum, quota, reservation, allocation, usage, service, and outcome remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Dominant shares use canonical allocatable totals; hierarchical shares are converted to a consistent parent or whole-cluster basis.

evidence: Executed simplified-dominant-share-allocation with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced alternating A/B assignments, final A=(9,3), B=(3,9), shares 0.75, and total (12,12).
Recomputed max-min demand example (2,5,20) over 12 as (2,5,5), and weighted split over 12 as (4,8).
Recomputed parent 60 percent with 2:1 children as 40/20 percent and Example 9 Jain index as 8/9.
Recomputed exercises: (3,7,7,7), weighted dominant shares A=0.20/B=0.40/C=0.20, hierarchy 40/20/10 percent, and Jain index 0.75.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Discrete fixtures illustrate accounting; they do not establish placement, temporal, strategic, or production outcome fairness.

evidence: Verified single-resource water filling does not exceed demand and equalizes remaining unsatisfied allocations under equal weights.
Checked dominant share is the maximum allocation fraction and weighted comparison divides by positive entitlement weight.
Verified hierarchical child shares multiply through the parent and cannot bypass ancestor maxima.
Checked Jain index bounds/equality interpretation applies only to consistently chosen normalized service inputs.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Simplified DRF properties are not generalized to heterogeneous placement, indivisible tasks, gangs, time, priorities, or arbitrary strategic reports.

evidence: Reviewed no/one/all active queues, demand below/at/above entitlement, zero/large weights, minima/maxima, borrowing, and capacity shrink.
Reviewed complementary/conflicting shapes, infeasible large tasks, rare devices, locality skips, reservations, gangs, and fragmentation.
Reviewed long non-preemptible borrowers, owner return, victim grace/failure, wrong-vector preemption, repeated victimization, and oscillation.
Reviewed identity/account splitting, forged queue/priority, inflated/understated requests, tiny-task gaming, stale policy, and telemetry privacy.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Allocation equality, entitlement, useful progress, starvation, placement, efficiency, security, and outcome fairness are reviewed independently.

evidence: Traced authenticated subjects through leaf/ancestor accounting, entitlement calculation, demand cap, feasible placement, allocation, borrowing, and release.
Checked children reconcile within every parent and resource partition while minima/maxima/user limits remain enforced.
Checked borrowed capacity stays marked reclaimable and owner restoration has completion/preemption timing semantics.
Checked preemption frees the right resource vector on a beneficiary-feasible node and accounts for state/retry/effect cost.
invariant_checking.notes: Instantaneous and temporal shares retain separate accounting, and inaccessible capacity is excluded from denominators.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from identity/contract through ideal shares, feasible placement, borrowing, starvation, preemption, security, and outcomes.
Checked the simplified progressive DRF argument stops at demand/resource bounds and remains work-conserving only when a feasible bundle exists.
Checked counterexamples for aggregate entitlement without node fit and preemption that frees unusable resources.
Checked high utilization or instantaneous equality is not used as proof of temporal fairness or acceptable latency.
proof_review.notes: Formal models, scheduler implementation, organizational policy, and empirical outcomes are clearly separated.

evidence: Audited fair, equal, weighted, dominant, guaranteed, entitled, instantaneous, steady, temporal, work-conserving, borrowed, starved, and preempted.
Confirmed every fairness claim names subject/resource/interval or explicitly identifies missing scope.
Confirmed configured capacity is not mislabeled physical reservation and borrowing is not mislabeled guarantee.
Confirmed DRF and Jain index are not mislabeled as complete production or normative fairness proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Priority, quota, fairness, capacity, and preemption preserve separate semantics.

evidence: Reviewed entitlement/demand/allocation/use, shares/deficits/borrowing, pending/starvation, preemption/restoration, locality/fragmentation, and victim metrics.
Confirmed no universal weights, capacities, fairness interval, delay threshold, preemption timeout, active-app limit, or fairness-index target is prescribed.
Confirmed executable allocation output is not evidence for heterogeneous placement, fairness over time, or user outcomes.
Confirmed production validation requires trace preservation, adversarial tenant mixtures, capacity/failure/policy perturbations, canary, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Allocation evidence is paired with completion/slowdown/deadline/freshness, efficiency, reliability, and cost outcomes.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed fairness contract, guarantees versus observations, max-min/weighted/DRF, hierarchy, steady/instant shares, borrowing, starvation, small jobs, temporal service, request incentives, locality, placement, gangs, priority, preemption, user limits, partitions, evidence, security, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable queue trees, capacity/weight/min/max/user controls, work-conserving lending, restoration objectives, locality delay, gang reservations, feasible victim selection, identity/priority governance, dashboards, trace replay, canaries, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from fairness definitions and arithmetic through hierarchical capacity and difficult placement/preemption cases. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover water filling, weights, dominant shares, hierarchy, fragmentation, locality, gangs, borrowing, Jain index, executable DRF, and production review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Hadoop/Spark/Mesos/Kubernetes/Borg maintainer, scheduling/mechanism-design researcher, organizational capacity owner, data-platform/SRE/FinOps/security specialist, affected tenant, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
